financial_anchor.caveat: Adjusted; +10% CER but -1% reported in CHF. IFRS operating profit was CHF9.7bn; FCF CHF4.2bn and net debt CHF22.071bn.

ai_claim.claim: Roche has deployed a 2,176-GPU AI estate and has an existing PathAI partnership intended for digital pathology and companion diagnostics.
ai_claim.scope: R&D compute and partnered pathology platform
ai_claim.limitation: Infrastructure is an input. Paige-led PRISM benchmarks are external competitor evidence, not Roche outcomes; no prospective productivity or retained cash result.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: Pathology foundation models from Paige and academia show model capability can diffuse, while Roche still had to agree up to $1.05bn for PathAI.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Regulated workflow integration and distribution may remain scarce even if models diffuse.

rights_limit: Patient, laboratory, slide and report rights are contract/consent specific; acquisition does not establish unrestricted pooled training rights.
materiality_summary: Five percent of H1 core operating profit is CHF595m for six months, or CHF1.19bn/year if mechanically annualized. Illustrative pathology contribution is CHF152m/year. A separate R&D present-value illustration cannot be used to fill the annual gap.

arithmetic.inputs: Annualized scale proxy CHF11.9bn×2×5%; pathology 20,000×CHF100k×40%×45%×70%−CHF100m/year; separate R&D PV 15×CHF250m×15%×80%
arithmetic.result: CHF1.19bn/year hurdle; CHF152m/year pathology; CHF450m one-time R&D PV, not directly comparable

g2_provisional: Insufficient/provisional: Roche has E2 infrastructure and partnership evidence only; external Paige benchmarks cannot support Roche. Quality-adjusted production and cash capture are absent.
unresolved_questions: What data licenses transfer with PathAI?
Which sites and case types use algorithms in production?
Which drug programmes were materially AI-selected?
